validity.recommendation: Attach the two independent refs below to Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location/Owner [ref] cells; no data change needed.
validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki 403'd (Cloudflare, matches scope note) so no leads from the row's own citations. Found two independent, non-GEM primary/technical sources that specifically name a Sawan-to-Qadirpur pipeline in Pakistan: (1) S.R. Lone (Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd) & R.P. Spiers (Energy Solutions International), 'Gas Transmission Development Strategy - a modeling approach', PSIG 2006 conference paper (hosted as a technical reference PDF on emerson.com) -- states verbatim: 'Sawan gas is transported through an 81-mile 24-inch pipeline to Qadirpur, and then independently of Qadirpur gas to Bhong compressor station (AC1X) via a 44-mile 30-inch pipeline,' in a section titled 'TRANSMISSION PIPELINE NETWORK' describing SNGPL's owned-and-operated system. (2) SNGPL's own May 2014 company newsletter (sngpl.com.pk) -- states 'The present capacity of Sawan-Qadirpur-Bhong segment excluding 42-dia x 22 KM pipeline (pipeline being laid between Sawan-Qadirpur section), is 310 MMCFD' while describing a THEN-PLANNED separate 42-inch augmentation pipeline for the same corridor. These two sources are independent of each other (different authors/publishers, 8 years apart, neither cites the other) and of GEM. EXISTENCE: confirmed -- this is a real, named SNGPL transmission segment, not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: confirmed -- explicitly described within SNGPL's 'transmission pipeline network' / 'transmission system,' matching PipelineType=transmission (not a gathering line). ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL)' 100% matches both sources exactly (source 1's author is an SNGPL employee describing SNGPL's own system; source 2 is SNGPL's own newsletter). Location: StartLocation=Sawan (Khairpur District, Sindh -- confirmed via Wikipedia's Sawan gas field article, operator OMV Pakistan historically / United Energy Pakistan since March 2018) and EndLocation=Qadirpur (near Ghotki, Sindh -- confirmed via Wikipedia's Qadirpur gas field article, operator OGDCL) both check out; both are in Sindh, matching GEM's Start/EndState=Sindh. SPEC: Diameter=24in matches source 1 exactly ('24-inch'). Length=131.00km vs source 1's '81-mile' (=130.36km) is a 0.64km / 0.49% difference -- immaterial rounding, not a material disagreement, so no spec concern flagged. Status=operating: both sources describe the line as part of the live, in-service network (2006 and 2014); Wikipedia additionally notes the Sawan field itself was still producing gas as of 'late 2023' (97% of recoverable reserves recovered by then), which requires this offtake line to still be in service -- reasonably current support for 'operating', though I found no post-2023 direct confirmation (web search quota was exhausted mid-task; relied on WebFetch to direct URLs/cached engines only). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 63-row roster: P4101 'SV1-QV1 Gas Pipeline' (Sawan->Sindh, len=130.77km, dia=42in) covers nearly the identical distance on the same Sawan-Qadirpur corridor but at a different (larger) diameter -- 'SV1'/'QV1' plausibly abbreviate Sawan Valve station 1 / Qadirpur Valve station 1. This is NOT a duplicate of P4079: source 2 (SNGPL 2014 newsletter) explicitly describes a NEW, separate 42-inch pipeline being built alongside/parallel to the existing Sawan-Qadirpur line for capacity augmentation -- i.e. P4079 (original, smaller-diameter, matches the 2006-documented existing line) and P4101 (newer parallel loop, matches the 2014-planned 42-inch project) are two distinct physical pipes in the same corridor, analogous to the Qadirpur Gas Pipeline / Qadirpur Gas Loopline pattern elsewhere in this roster. Flagging for context only -- no action needed on P4079; P4101 should get its own scrutiny in its own audit pass to confirm it isn't itself double-counted against some other roster row. Capacity was left blank: the only capacity figure found (310 MMCFD, later 350 MMCFD) is stated for the combined 'Sawan-Qadirpur-Bhong segment' (i.e. this 24in line PLUS the separate 44-mile 30in Qadirpur-Bhong continuation per source 1), not cleanly attributable to the Sawan-Qadirpur leg alone -- per instructions, left blank rather than fabricating a segment-specific number.

summary: P4079 confirmed real, correctly classified SNGPL transmission line (Sawan->Qadirpur, Sindh, 24in/~131km, operator SNGPL) via two independent primary sources (PSIG 2006 paper + SNGPL's own May 2014 newsletter); not a duplicate of the separate parallel 42in P4101 loop. Capacity left UNRESOLVED/blank (only a combined-segment MMCFD figure found, not attributable to this leg alone).
